findings.reason: the node as written cannot be built within its declared write paths (`promotion_evidence.py` and the new test); it must either add the fields and the CLI surface (`reckon_run_commands.py`, `reckon/ledger.py`) to the scope or name where the asserted figures come from.
findings.text: §7 requires `_require_gate_log_agrees` to refuse "a passing gate whose asserted failure count differs from the cited log's last pytest summary, or whose failure ids differ from the log's `FAILED` lines", but a gate check is built from `--gate-command`, `--gate-exit-status`, `--gate-log-path` and `--gate-log-digest` only (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:221-226) and `_normalized_gate_check` stores exactly `command`, `exit_status`, `log_path` and `log_digest` (reckon/ledger.py:482-487); there is no asserted count or ids anywhere in the promotion evidence, so the comparison has no left-hand side and the section's own qualifier "a gate check that asserts no count or ids is judged on exit status alone, as today" describes every gate check that exists today

findings.reason: a done-when whose case already fails at base cannot show the new count/ids comparison fires, and its negative controls assert a flip the case cannot produce; the case must name a receipt carrying the last run's exit status with the first run's count or ids.
findings.text: §7's first case is "a log holding a passing run then a failing run, with a receipt copied from the first, is refused naming the count and the ids", while its first two negative controls require that dropping the count comparison, or reading the first run's summary, makes the first case pass; a receipt copied from the first run also carries the first run's exit status, and the existing exit-status check reads the log's tail (reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:1117-1132), so the unfixed code already refuses that receipt on status and neither control can flip it

findings.reason: a worker told to read `steps.land.merge` finds no such field and must guess between `commit` and `remote_head`, and `remote_head` is set only after a push, so the fallback does not cover a landing whose push is outstanding.
findings.text: §6's deliverable judges the worktree "against the merge commit the landing recorded (`steps.land.merge` or `remote_head`)", but the landing report has no `merge` key: merge.py builds `{base, head, commit, branch, remote, pushed}` and adds `remote_head` after the push (reckon/crew/merge.py:783-793), and `steps.land` is that report with an `ok` flag (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3336); the merge commit is recorded as `commit`

findings.reason: `s7` and `s4` are both unlocked once §2 lands, so the queue can launch them concurrently on the same file, which the one-worker-one-file rule forbids; the wait must be declared on §4.
findings.text: §7 closes with "It shares `promotion_evidence.py` with §2, §4 and §5, so it waits for §5", but §5 declares `promotion_checks.py`, `ledger.py`, `landing_measure.py` and its test as its write paths and never touches `promotion_evidence.py`, so the declared wait orders §7 behind a section that does not contend the file; the actual co-writer §4 declares `promotion_evidence.py` as a write path and is not upstream of §7 (its only declared wait is on §2, as is §5's)

findings.reason: it is an orientation declaration no node's scope or gate reads, but a coordinator dispatching from it would under-count the plan's work by three sections.
findings.text: `plan-standalone` still reads "It repairs two checks inside crew complete, the red-base id match and the commit coverage", while the plan now carries §5 (three further comparison sites), §6 (the worktree release audit) and §7 (gate receipt versus log) as implementable sections

response_events.note: §7 now names its left-hand side: the manifest's after_suite arm (exit_status, failure_count, failure_ids), read as _zero_added_against_a_red_base reads it, against the cited gate log.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §6 names `steps.land.merge`, a key the landing record does not carry; `reckon/crew/merge.py:783-793` records `base`, `head`, `commit`, `branch`, `remote`, `pushed` and `remote_head`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §7's first case and its first two negative controls contradict each other, so the headline case does not exercise the check the section adds.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §6 requires every log under the run directory with its revision, command and a closing `EXIT=` line; §7's temporary logs are in-test fixtures, not gate evidence.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames name the behaviour (`test_a_landed_head_releases_its_worktree.py`, `test_a_receipt_agrees_with_its_log.py`) and no ticket number, plan label or version tag enters a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's mechanism compares the gate check's "asserted failure count" and "asserted failure ids" against the log, but no gate check carries either field, and the section's write paths cannot add them.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 states one deliverable (the release audit judges the landed merge commit instead of `HEAD`) and §7 one (the gate receipt's count and ids agree with its log).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §7 declares `plan-section-depends-on` on §5 and says it shares `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py` "with §2, §4 and §5", but §5's write paths do not include that file and the co-writer it must serialise against, §4, is not upstream of §7.
